page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-48GB is a KVM-hypervised virtual server belonging to the Cloud Native family. It features 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 12.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear tradeoff between memory capacity and processing speed. The shared AMD EPYC CPU delivers poor single-core performance in stress-ng testing and weak multi-core performance in Geekbench. Large-block memory bandwidth read and write speeds are also weak, though small-block cached reads reach an average speed of 411.75 GB/sec. The server demonstrates average performance in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, alongside average scores in PassMark CPU tests and Redis SET operations.

This hardware profile offers a cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated CPU performance. The high memory density relative to the shared CPU allocation makes it suitable for caching layers, lightweight database operations, text processing, and small-scale language model inference. However, it is less optimal for CPU-bound tasks like software compilation, ray tracing, or large-scale web serving due to its shared CPU limits and weak multi-core scaling.
